[*]Press Windows + R to show a 'run' dialogue box.
[*]Paste this exact text:platformpath

[/list]Linux
[list=1]
[*]The root directory for save files is specified by the XDG_CONFIG_HOME environment variable, which defaults to ~/.config/
[*]From [i]Files[/i], click [i]Go » Enter Location[/i].
[*]Enter this exact text:~/.config/StardewValley/Saves
[*]Submit to open the folder.
[/list]Mac[list=1]
[*]From [i]Finder[/i], click [i]Go » Go to Folder[/i].
[*]Enter this exact text:~/.config/StardewValley/Saves
[*]Submit to open the folder.
[/list]Mobile (Android)[list=1]
[*]Open your device's file explorer app. If your device does not come with a file explorer, you will need one that allows navigation of the internal storage, not just searching for a specific file.
[*]Select the Android/data/com.chucklefish.stardewvalley/files/saves (version 1.5 or later) or StardewValley (before 1.5) folder.
[*]Each subfolder inside with a name in the format of JonSnow_123456789 is a save slot.
[/list]Mobile (iOS)[list=1]
[*]Open the Files app.
[*]On iPhone, tap the [i]Browse[/i] button on the bottom-right side of the screen. On iPad, tap the top-left button if needed to show the left sidebar menu.
[*]Under the Locations section, tap [i]On My iPhone/iPad[/i].
[*]Select the [i]Stardew Valley[/i] folder.
[*]Each subfolder inside with a name like JonSnow_123456789 is a save slot.
[/list]On iOS 12 or earlier:Devices still on iOS 12 or earlier will need to be connected to a Mac or Windows computer to access your save files.
[list=1]
[*]On Mac, Open the Finder. On Windows, [url=https://support.apple.com/en-us/HT210384]download iTunes[/url] and open it. (If your device is on macOS 10.14 or earlier, open iTunes instead of the Finder.)
[*]Attach your iOS device via USB.
[*]In the Finder/iTunes, click on the device icon in the top toolbar. (If the icon isn't shown, try disconnecting and reconnecting the USB cable.) The device's page should appear.
[*]Click [i]File Sharing[/i] in the menu on the left.
[*]Click [i]Stardew Valley[/i] in the app list that appears.
[*]The [i]Stardew Valley Documents[/i] panel shows which save files are already on your iOS device. (They appear as folders, but you can't navigate into the folders directly.)
[/list]PS VitaNote: Access to the Vita filesystem requires custom firmware (CFW)
[list=1]
[*]Navigate to [code]ux0:/user/00/savedata/[/code]
 in Vita Shell.
[*]Highlight the PCSE01235 folder and press triangle.
[*]Select "Open decrypted" at the top of the list.
[/list]Nintendo SwitchNote: Access to a Switch's saves requires custom firmware (CFW)
[list=1]
[*]Download and install [url=https://github.com/J-D-K/JKSV/releases]JKSV[/url]
[*]Open JKSV and navigate to Stardew Valley.
[*]Select New, and call it whatever you want.
[*]In either the Hekate SD card access tool or an FTP server, copy over [code]sd:/JKSV/Stardew Valley/NameOfTheSaveYouSaved.zip[/code]
